simple.meaning: קַנָּא (qannâʼ) is a Hebrew word meaning “jealous.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: קַנָּא (H7067) appears 6 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Exodus 20:5, with occurrences in Exodus, Deuteronomy.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to קַנָּא (H7067) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in קַנָּא (H7067) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: קַנָּא (qannâʼ) / H7067 is traced through Exodus 20:5, Exodus 34:14, Deuteronomy 4:24, Deuteronomy 5:9 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H7067. qanna קַנָּא adjective jealous ; — only of God: קַנָּא אֵל Exod 20:5 (J) = Deut 5:9 (as punishing those who hate him), Exod 34:14 (J), Deut 4:24 ; 6:15 (demanding exclusive service); שְׁמוֺ קַנָּא Exod 34:14 (J).
